examples.title: Fake PayPal Verification Email
examples.description: Instead of clicking the link, type paypal.com directly into your browser and log in there to check your account status.

examples.title: Fake Package Delivery Email
examples.description: Look up your tracking number directly on the carrier's official site or app rather than clicking the link in the email.

examples.title: Fake Shared Document Email
examples.description: Go directly to the file-sharing service's own site or app to check for shared files, instead of clicking the link in the email.

examples.title: Fake “Boss” Gift Card Request
examples.description: Call or message the person directly using a number or channel you already know is theirs, rather than replying to the email.

examples.title: Fake Unusual Login Alert
examples.description: Log into your account directly through the official site or app to check recent activity, instead of clicking the link in the alert.

examples.title: Fake Benefits Enrollment Email
examples.description: Log into your company's actual HR or benefits portal directly to check your enrollment status, instead of clicking the link.

examples.title: Fake Government Agency Email
examples.description: Look up the agency's official phone number yourself and call to verify any balance, rather than using contact info from the email.

examples.title: Fake Prize Notification
examples.description: If you don't remember entering, you didn't win anything — a real prize never requires paying a fee upfront to receive it.

examples.title: Fake Password Expiration Notice
examples.description: Change your password by going directly to your company's real login page, not through a link in an unexpected email.

examples.title: Fake Law Enforcement Extortion Email
examples.description: Look up the agency's official number yourself and call to verify — real agencies never collect fines by email or in cryptocurrency.

examples.title: Fake Subscription Renewal Notice
examples.description: Check your billing status by logging into the service's official site or app directly, instead of clicking the link in the email.

examples.title: Fake Mailbox Storage Warning
examples.description: Check your real storage usage by logging into your email account directly through your provider's site or app.

examples.title: Fake Cloud Storage Payment Failure
examples.description: Log into the real storage provider's site or app directly to check your billing status, instead of clicking the link.

examples.title: Fake Inheritance / Advance-Fee Letter
examples.description: Don't reply or engage — a stranger offering a fortune from nowhere is never real, no matter how detailed or emotional the story.

examples.title: Fake Retailer Survey Prize Email
examples.description: Check the retailer's real site or app directly for any active promotions, rather than clicking the link or the unsubscribe button.

examples.title: Fake PayPal Account Limited Email
examples.description: Type paypal.com directly into your browser and log in there to check your account status, instead of clicking the link.

examples.title: Fake Zoom Meeting Attendees Email
examples.description: Open the Zoom app directly to start or check a meeting, rather than clicking a meeting link from an unexpected email.

examples.title: Fake FedEx Shipping Confirmation Email
examples.description: Look up your tracking number directly on FedEx's real site or app, rather than clicking the link or code in the email.

examples.title: Fake Facebook Password Reset Email
examples.description: Go directly to facebook.com yourself to check or change your password, and never enter a reset code on a page you clicked to from an email.
